answer: Identities registering during the same window share a hollow reputation curve, so faking thousands of accounts yields no advantage over one real agent. Each agent must stake a bond that decays toward a nadir over epochs; honest work replenishes it, while sybils splitting identities face a gale of cumulative slashing costs. An attacker must fund every duplicate with fresh capital and sustain it through challenge rounds, making the marginal cost of each fake identity exceed the reward it could ever capture. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
